Status light

A solid white light means the router is online and working normally. A pulsing blue light means the router is in setup mode and waiting for the app. A solid amber light means the router is powered on but has no internet connection. A flashing red light means a hardware fault or a failed firmware update; check the error code in the app.

What's in the box

The Q3 box contains the Q3 router, a 12 V power adapter, a 1.5 metre Ethernet cable, and a quick-start card. Satellite nodes are sold separately.
Quillon Q3 Mesh Router: Setup Guide

Version 4.1.3 (June 2026)

Fixes a problem where the status light stayed amber after the internet connection came back. Improves parental controls scheduling.

Adding satellite nodes

A Q3 network supports up to 6 satellite nodes in addition to the main router. Place each node no more than two rooms or about 10 metres from the router or from another node. In the app, go to Devices, then Add node, and follow the steps.

Before you contact us

Have your device's serial number ready; it is printed on the bottom of the device and shown in the app under Devices. For router problems, note the colour of the status light and any error code shown in the app.
Q3 Firmware Release Notes

Security settings

New Q3 networks use WPA3 encryption by default. If an older device cannot connect, turn on WPA2 compatibility mode under Settings, then Wi-Fi, then Security.

Router and node errors

E-101: No WAN cable detected. Make sure the Ethernet cable from your modem is plugged into the yellow WAN port, not one of the grey LAN ports.

E-102: Internet login failed. Your internet provider uses PPPoE and rejected the username or password. Re-enter the PPPoE username and password from your provider under Settings, then Internet.

E-204: The router did not receive an IP address from the modem. Restart the modem first, wait two minutes, then restart the router.

E-310: A satellite node lost its connection to the router. Move the node closer to the router or to another node, then wait five minutes for it to reconnect.

E-4012: The cooling fan has stopped. Turn the router off and contact support to arrange a replacement under warranty. Do not leave the router running with a stopped fan.

E-5020: The power supply is overheating. Unplug the router for one hour, move it away from heat sources, and make sure the vents are not covered.

E-7001: A firmware update failed its integrity check. The router automatically keeps its previous firmware. The update is retried after 30 minutes; if it fails three times in a row, contact support.

Free trial

Every new Q3 router includes a 30-day free trial of Secure Plus. You will not be charged if you cancel before the trial ends.

First-time setup

Connect the yellow WAN port on the back of the Q3 to your modem with the included Ethernet cable, then plug in the power adapter. Install the Quillon Home app on your phone and sign in or create an account. On your phone, join the Wi-Fi network named Quillon-Setup followed by the last four characters of the serial number, then follow the steps in the app. Setup usually takes about ten minutes.

How updates are installed

Routers install new firmware automatically between 2 a.m. and 4 a.m. local time. Updates are released gradually, so it can take up to two weeks before every router receives a new version.

Automatic updates

The Q3 checks for firmware updates every night and installs them automatically between 3 a.m. and 5 a.m. local time. You can postpone an update for up to 7 days in the app.

Restarting and factory reset

To restart the router, unplug the power adapter, wait 30 seconds, and plug it back in. Restarting keeps all of your settings.

To restore factory settings, press and hold the recessed reset button on the back of the router with a paperclip for 10 seconds, until the light starts pulsing blue. A factory reset erases your Wi-Fi name, password, guest network, and parental controls, and you will need to set up the router again in the app.

Error Codes Reference

The Quillon Home app shows an error code when a router, node, or camera reports a problem. Look up the code below before contacting support.

Setting up the camera

Plug the QC2 into power with the included USB-C cable and adapter. In the Quillon Home app, go to Devices, then Add camera, and scan the QR code on the back of the camera. The QC2 connects to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only; it cannot join a 5 GHz network.

Version 4.2.1 (October 2026)

Fixes the known issue in 4.2.0 where devices on the guest network were disconnected every 24 hours. Improves the stability of satellite nodes after a power cut.

If many customers are affected by an outage, we post updates on the Quillon status page and in the app's notification centre.

Router and node errors

E-101: No WAN cable detected. Make sure the Ethernet cable from your modem is plugged into the yellow WAN port, not one of the grey LAN ports.

E-204: The router did not receive an IP address from the modem. Restart the modem first, wait two minutes, then restart the router.

E-310: A satellite node lost its connection to the router. Move the node closer to the router or to another node, then wait five minutes for it to reconnect.

E-4012: The cooling fan has stopped. Turn the router off and contact support to arrange a replacement under warranty. Do not leave the router running with a stopped fan.

E-5020: The power supply is overheating. Unplug the router for one hour, move it away from heat sources, and make sure the vents are not covered.

E-7001: A firmware update failed its integrity check. The router automatically keeps its previous firmware. The update is retried after 30 minutes; if it fails three times in a row, contact support.

The account owner can invite up to 5 household members under Account, then Household. Household members can view cameras and manage Wi-Fi, but only the owner can change the subscription or delete the account.

Guest network

You can turn on a guest network in the app under Settings, then Wi-Fi, then Guest network. Devices on the guest network can reach the internet but cannot see devices on your main network. Up to 32 devices can use the guest network at the same time.

Camera errors

C-12: The camera does not recognise the microSD card. Use a card of 256 GB or less, formatted as exFAT.

C-31: The camera could not upload a recording to the cloud. Check that the camera is online and that your Quillon Secure plan includes cloud recording.

C-44: The camera is too far from the router. Move the camera or add a satellite node nearby.

Security settings

New Q3 networks use WPA3 encryption by default. If an older device cannot connect, turn on WPA2 compatibility mode under Settings, then Wi-Fi, then Security.

First-time setup

Connect the yellow WAN port on the back of the Q3 to your modem with the included Ethernet cable, then plug in the power adapter. Install the Quillon Home app on your phone and sign in or create an account. On your phone, join the Wi-Fi network named Quillon-Setup followed by the last four characters of the serial number, then follow the steps in the app. Setup usually takes about ten minutes.

Night vision and motion detection

Night vision works up to 10 metres in complete darkness. You can draw up to 4 motion zones in the app, and the camera only alerts you about motion inside those zones.

Restarting and factory reset

To restart the router, unplug the power adapter, wait 30 seconds, and plug it back in. Restarting keeps all of your settings.

To restore factory settings, press and hold the recessed reset button on the back of the router with a paperclip for 10 seconds, until the light starts pulsing blue. A factory reset erases your Wi-Fi name, password, guest network, and parental controls, and you will need to set up the router again in the app.

Router and node errors

E-101: No WAN cable detected. Make sure the Ethernet cable from your modem is plugged into the yellow WAN port, not one of the grey LAN ports.

E-102: Internet login failed. Your internet provider uses PPPoE and rejected the username or password. Re-enter the PPPoE username and password from your provider under Settings, then Internet.

E-204: The router did not receive an IP address from the modem. Restart the modem first, wait two minutes, then restart the router.

E-310: A satellite node lost its connection to the router. Move the node closer to the router or to another node, then wait five minutes for it to reconnect.

E-4012: The cooling fan has stopped. Turn the router off and contact support to arrange a replacement under warranty. Do not leave the router running with a stopped fan.

E-5020: The power supply is overheating. Unplug the router for one hour, move it away from heat sources, and make sure the vents are not covered.

E-7001: A firmware update failed its integrity check. The router automatically keeps its previous firmware. The update is retried after 30 minutes; if it fails three times in a row, contact support.

Recording and storage

The QC2 can record to a microSD card of up to 256 GB, which you insert in the slot underneath the camera. With a Quillon Secure Plus plan, recordings are also kept in the cloud for 14 days.

What's in the box

The Q3 box contains the Q3 router, a 12 V power adapter, a 1.5 metre Ethernet cable, and a quick-start card. Satellite nodes are sold separately.

Status light

A solid white light means the router is online and working normally. A pulsing blue light means the router is in setup mode and waiting for the app. A solid amber light means the router is powered on but has no internet connection. A flashing red light means a hardware fault or a failed firmware update; check the error code in the app.

The Quillon Home app shows an error code when a router, node, or camera reports a problem. Look up the code below before contacting support.

Status light

A solid white light means the router is online and working normally. A pulsing blue light means the router is in setup mode and waiting for the app. A solid amber light means the router is powered on but has no internet connection. A flashing red light means a hardware fault or a failed firmware update; check the error code in the app.

Before you contact us

Have your device's serial number ready; it is printed on the bottom of the device and shown in the app under Devices. For router problems, note the colour of the status light and any error code shown in the app.

C-12: The camera does not recognise the microSD card. Use a card of 256 GB or less, formatted as exFAT.

C-31: The camera could not upload a recording to the cloud. Check that the camera is online and that your Quillon Secure plan includes cloud recording.

C-44: The camera is too far from the router. Move the camera or add a satellite node nearby.

E-204: The router did not receive an IP address from the modem. Restart the modem first, wait two minutes, then restart the router.

E-310: A satellite node lost its connection to the router. Move the node closer to the router or to another node, then wait five minutes for it to reconnect.

E-4012: The cooling fan has stopped. Turn the router off and contact support to arrange a replacement under warranty. Do not leave the router running with a stopped fan.

E-5020: The power supply is overheating. Unplug the router for one hour, move it away from heat sources, and make sure the vents are not covered.

E-7001: A firmware update failed its integrity check. The router automatically keeps its previous firmware. The update is retried after 30 minutes; if it fails three times in a row, contact support.

Restarting and factory reset

To restart the router, unplug the power adapter, wait 30 seconds, and plug it back in. Restarting keeps all of your settings.

To restore factory settings, press and hold the recessed reset button on the back of the router with a paperclip for 10 seconds, until the light starts pulsing blue. A factory reset erases your Wi-Fi name, password, guest network, and parental controls, and you will need to set up the router again in the app.

Resetting the camera

To reset the QC2 to factory settings, press and hold the reset button underneath the camera for 5 seconds, until it plays a chime. You will then need to add the camera in the app again.

Router and node errors

E-101: No WAN cable detected. Make sure the Ethernet cable from your modem is plugged into the yellow WAN port, not one of the grey LAN ports.

E-102: Internet login failed. Your internet provider uses PPPoE and rejected the username or password. Re-enter the PPPoE username and password from your provider under Settings, then Internet.

E-204: The router did not receive an IP address from the modem. Restart the modem first, wait two minutes, then restart the router.

E-310: A satellite node lost its connection to the router. Move the node closer to the router or to another node, then wait five minutes for it to reconnect.

E-4012: The cooling fan has stopped. Turn the router off and contact support to arrange a replacement under warranty. Do not leave the router running with a stopped fan.

E-5020: The power supply is overheating. Unplug the router for one hour, move it away from heat sources, and make sure the vents are not covered.

E-7001: A firmware update failed its integrity check. The router automatically keeps its previous firmware. The update is retried after 30 minutes; if it fails three times in a row, contact support.

Night vision works up to 10 metres in complete darkness. You can draw up to 4 motion zones in the app, and the camera only alerts you about motion inside those zones.

Restarting and factory reset

To restart the router, unplug the power adapter, wait 30 seconds, and plug it back in. Restarting keeps all of your settings.

To restore factory settings, press and hold the recessed reset button on the back of the router with a paperclip for 10 seconds, until the light starts pulsing blue. E-204: The router did not receive an IP address from the modem. Restart the modem first, wait two minutes, then restart the router.

E-310: A satellite node lost its connection to the router. Move the node closer to the router or to another node, then wait five minutes for it to reconnect.

E-4012: The cooling fan has stopped. Turn the router off and contact support to arrange a replacement under warranty. Do not leave the router running with a stopped fan.

First-time setup

Connect the yellow WAN port on the back of the Q3 to your modem with the included Ethernet cable, then plug in the power adapter. Install the Quillon Home app on your phone and sign in or create an account. On your phone, join the Wi-Fi network named Quillon-Setup followed by the last four characters of the serial number, then follow the steps in the app. Setup usually takes about ten minutes.

Automatic updates

The Q3 checks for firmware updates every night and installs them automatically between 3 a.m. and 5 a.m. local time. You can postpone an update for up to 7 days in the app.

Router and node errors

E-101: No WAN cable detected. Make sure the Ethernet cable from your modem is plugged into the yellow WAN port, not one of the grey LAN ports.

E-102: Internet login failed. Your internet provider uses PPPoE and rejected the username or password. Re-enter the PPPoE username and password from your provider under Settings, then Internet.

E-204: The router did not receive an IP address from the modem. Restart the modem first, wait two minutes, then restart the router.

E-310: A satellite node lost its connection to the router. Move the node closer to the router or to another node, then wait five minutes for it to reconnect.

E-4012: The cooling fan has stopped. Turn the router off and contact support to arrange a replacement under warranty. Do not leave the router running with a stopped fan.

E-5020: The power supply is overheating. Unplug the router for one hour, move it away from heat sources, and make sure the vents are not covered.

E-7001: A firmware update failed its integrity check. The router automatically keeps its previous firmware. The update is retried after 30 minutes; if it fails three times in a row, contact support.

Status light

A solid white light means the router is online and working normally. A pulsing blue light means the router is in setup mode and waiting for the app. A solid amber light means the router is powered on but has no internet connection. A flashing red light means a hardware fault or a failed firmware update; check the error code in the app.

Before you contact us

Have your device's serial number ready; it is printed on the bottom of the device and shown in the app under Devices. For router problems, note the colour of the status light and any error code shown in the app.

Error Codes Reference

The Quillon Home app shows an error code when a router, node, or camera reports a problem. Look up the code below before contacting support.

How updates are installed

Routers install new firmware automatically between 2 a.m. and 4 a.m. local time. Updates are released gradually, so it can take up to two weeks before every router receives a new version.

Restarting and factory reset

To restart the router, unplug the power adapter, wait 30 seconds, and plug it back in. Restarting keeps all of your settings.

To restore factory settings, press and hold the recessed reset button on the back of the router with a paperclip for 10 seconds, until the light starts pulsing blue. A factory reset erases your Wi-Fi name, password, guest network, and parental controls, and you will need to set up the router again in the app.

C-31: The camera could not upload a recording to the cloud. Check that the camera is online and that your Quillon Secure plan includes cloud recording.

C-44: The camera is too far from the router. Move the camera or add a satellite node nearby.

Setting up the camera

Plug the QC2 into power with the included USB-C cable and adapter. In the Quillon Home app, go to Devices, then Add camera, and scan the QR code on the back of the camera. The QC2 connects to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only; it cannot join a 5 GHz network.
